title: Resonance Lab
notConnected: Connect to your machine to check for an accelerometer.
accelMissing: No accelerometer found in the object model. Configure one with M955 to run measurements.
accelSetupHint: Board {address} ({board}) has an SPI accelerometer — chip-select pin first, then interrupt. Add this to config.g:
overflows: The accelerometer reported {count} sample overflow(s) — results may be unreliable. Try a lower sample rate (M955) or a shorter run.
notHomed: Home all axes before measuring — the test shakes the machine and needs a known position.

accel.rateHelp: Records about 100 stationary samples and reads the sampling rate the firmware writes into the file — the rate every analysis here is computed against. It can differ from the M955 S value you asked for: the chip only has a few fixed output rates and the firmware rounds the request to one of them. For example a LIS3DH at 10- or 12-bit resolution runs at 1344 Hz (it only offers 1600 Hz in 8-bit mode), while a LIS2DW or LIS3DSH settles on 400, 800 or 1600 Hz. No motion, so no homing is needed.
accel.rateCheckFailed: Couldn't read the accelerometer's sampling rate: {reason}
accel.toolNotActive: This accelerometer is on the toolboard of {tool}, which isn't the active tool — pick up {tool} first (it may be parked), otherwise the accelerometer isn't on the carriage and the measurement is meaningless.
accel.wiringMissing: This accelerometer's wiring isn't recorded anywhere yet — run the orientation task with it active, then save it, to make it selectable here.

emptyHint: Set the options above and press Measure — or load a previous capture CSV.

controls.customMoves: Custom move profile (one G-code per line)

settings.title: Resonance Lab settings
settings.programDirHint: Where generated test G-code files are uploaded (e.g. sweep/belt programs) — kept separate from 0:/sys's own config/homing files. Captured CSV results always go to 0:/sys/accelerometer (fixed by the firmware).
settings.programDirNote: Captured measurement data itself always lands in 0:/sys/accelerometer — that location is set by the firmware and can't be changed. This setting only controls where the plugin's own generated test programs are uploaded.

orientation.underdetermined: Couldn't fully determine the orientation — ensure the X and Y moves actually moved the toolhead and re-run.
orientation.conflict: The {axes} move excited the same sensor channel as another axis — frame coupling (bedslinger?) or loose mounting.
orientation.coupling: High cross-axis coupling ({pct}%) — check the accelerometer is rigidly mounted.
orientation.applied: Orientation applied (I{i}). Add the M955 I parameter to config.g to keep it.
orientation.wiringMissing: This accelerometer's wiring isn't recorded anywhere yet — run this check with it active, then save it, before measuring or applying an orientation.

belts.notCoreXY: Belt comparison needs CoreXY-style kinematics (diagonal belt paths). Your machine reports a different kinematics type.
belts.phaseTiming: first run at these settings — establishing the real motion time, reused next time
belts.matchedDetail: Both belts resonate alike (peaks {peakA} / {peakB} Hz) with balanced energy — no tension adjustment needed.
belts.tensionDetail: The spectra share a shape but {louder} carries {ratio}× the vibration energy — adjust belt tension and re-run.
belts.mismatchDetail: Different resonances ({peakA} vs {peakB} Hz) point at a mechanical difference — check pulleys, idlers and belt paths, not just tension.

profile.cleanDetail: Vibration stays near the baseline across the tested speed range.
profile.problemsDetail: These speeds excite a resonance (≥2× the baseline). Quietest tested speeds: {quiet}.

motor.cleanDetail: Vibration at every checked harmonic stays low across the tested speed range.
motor.noMotor: No drivable motor found on this axis configuration.
motor.noSpeeds: None of the planned speeds produced an analysable recording — try a lower maximum speed or a longer move.

findings.fullStep: {motor} motor: full-step vibration up to {um} um at {hz} Hz ({level}), caused by detent torque and step ripple
findings.phase: {motor} motor: the component with a period of two full steps reaches {um} um at {hz} Hz, {ratio}% of the full-step vibration ({level}) — indicates a current imbalance between the two coils
findings.waveform: {motor} motor: components with a period of one electrical cycle reach {um} um at {hz} Hz, {ratio}% of the full-step vibration ({level}) — indicate a distorted current waveform

motorTune.chipUnknown: Could not identify the chip — relying on the driver's own response
motorTune.chipUnsupported: {chip} does not support waveform correction — a TMC5160 or TMC2240 is required
motorTune.stepDirHint: This driver uses its sine table, so harmonic 2 (coil imbalance) can't be corrected — enable phase stepping with M970 (or closed loop, on a board that supports it) to tune it too.
motorTune.status: Measuring harmonic {h} at magnitude {mag}°, phase {phase}° — move {n}/{total}

lock.unsteady: The vibration frequency the analysis locked onto kept disagreeing between recordings ({count} had to be accepted anyway after retaking them), so the readings of narrow orders may be unreliable. Re-run on a quiet machine, or try a different test speed.
lock.offNominal: The analysis found the motor's full-step vibration at {found} Hz, {percent}% away from the {expected} Hz the commanded speed should produce. Check the axis steps/mm and microstepping, and that the accelerometer really samples at its configured rate.

motorTune.statusCheckOff: Checking: measuring with the corrections off…
motorTune.statusCheckOn: Checking: measuring with the corrections on…
motorTune.phaseModeNote: This axis is in step/dir mode, and a correction only acts in phase stepping — so the run switches the axis into phase stepping (M970) and back again afterwards. To keep a result, add M970 to config.g as well; the result lists the line.
motorTune.phaseModeFailed: Couldn't switch axis {axis} into phase stepping (M970): {reply}
motorTune.surveyHint: Run this first. Five back-to-back moves measure all 16 harmonics on the uncorrected motor and rank them by how far each stands above the background and how repeatable its reading is: a weak order can read several times higher or lower from one capture to the next, and a correction can't be told apart from that. A driver can hold only 4 corrections at once, so the 4 best are chosen for you and the other chips stay greyed out. Harmonics above the accelerometer's Nyquist frequency at this speed can't be seen at all.
motorTune.surveyFirst: Run the survey first. Until it has run, every harmonic is greyed out: it measures all 16 five times and picks the 4 worth tuning.
motorTune.surveyDone: Survey done. A driver can only hold 4 corrections at once, so the 4 most repeatable strong harmonics have been chosen: {list}. The rest are greyed out — tick “Choose manually” to override.
motorTune.surveyFew: Survey done. Only {n} harmonic(s) stood clear of the background at this speed, so only those are chosen: {list}. The rest are greyed out — tick “Choose manually” to override.
motorTune.surveyNone: Survey done, but no harmonic stood clear of the background at this speed, so none is offered. Try a different speed, or tick “Choose manually”.
motorTune.surveyUnmeasured: {n} harmonics were not measured at all, because they sit above the accelerometer's Nyquist frequency at this speed — that is not the same as being quiet. A test speed of about {speed} mm/s or lower brings S1–S8 into reach; run the survey again there to check them.
motorTune.surveyStale: The survey was taken for a different motor, speed or length and no longer applies — run it again.
motorTune.manualHint: Lifts the survey restriction so you can pick any harmonics yourself. The physical limits stay: at most 4 at once, and nothing above the accelerometer's Nyquist frequency.
motorTune.manualNote: Manual mode: the survey is not being used. Pick up to 4 harmonics; ones that carry no signal at this speed will simply report no improvement.

chipReason.notTop: Not one of the 4 best harmonics in the survey (a driver holds only 4 corrections)
chipReason.unstable: Strong enough, but the reading scatters too much from one capture to the next for a correction's effect to be told apart from it
chipReason.nyquist: Above the accelerometer's Nyquist frequency at this speed - can't be measured

motorTune.harmonicsHint: S is the firmware's harmonic of the electrical cycle (four full steps), so S/4 is the order in full steps: S2 coil gain imbalance, S4 waveform distortion and detent, the rest higher-order distortion. A driver holds at most 4 corrections at once.
motorTune.skipNyquist: Harmonic(s) {list} would sit above the accelerometer's Nyquist frequency at this speed — reduce the speed to {speed} mm/s or below, or deselect them.
motorTune.skipSlots: Harmonic(s) {list} don't fit: a driver holds at most {max} corrections at once, counting any it already has that you aren't tuning — deselect {list}.
motorTune.tooMany: A driver holds at most {max} corrections at once — deselect {n} harmonic(s) to measure.

diagnostics.hint: Saves a JSON file with every survey, tune and verify capture from this session: each order's reading per move direction, the corrections live on the driver at the time, the frequency the analysis located, and the motor, speed and firmware details. Held in memory only — it is gone when the page reloads. Nothing is uploaded.

motorTune.checkHint: Measures the motor twice back to back — once with the corrections from this result switched off, once with them on — and compares each tuned harmonic. This confirms the corrections really are what removes the vibration. The driver is put back exactly as it was found, so it works whether you kept the result or not. A change under 20% is treated as scatter.

check.headlineBetter: Verified: the corrections reduce the vibration.
check.headlineWorse: With the corrections on, at least one harmonic is worse than with them off — run the tune again or discard.
check.headlineUnchanged: No meaningful difference between the corrections on and off.
check.better: Harmonic {h}: {off} g off → {on} g on, {percent}% lower
check.worse: Harmonic {h}: {off} g off → {on} g on, {percent}% higher
check.unchanged: Harmonic {h}: {off} g off → {on} g on, no meaningful change

motorTune.dropped: Harmonic {h}: dropped. Its search measured {searched} (uncorrected {before}), but with every correction in place it read {after}. The corrections may disturb each other, or this order's readings may simply scatter from one capture to the next. It is switched off again.
motorTune.droppedKept: Harmonic {h}: dropped. Its search measured {searched} (uncorrected {before}), but with every correction in place it read {after}. The corrections may disturb each other, or this order's readings may simply scatter from one capture to the next. It keeps the correction the driver already had.
motorTune.noImprovementKept: Harmonic {h}: no correction improved the vibration, so it keeps the correction the driver already had
motorTune.noImprovement: Harmonic {h}: no correction improved the vibration, it stays disabled
motorTune.withinScatterKept: Harmonic {h}: the best correction gained less than this order's own capture-to-capture scatter ({spread}), so it is not adopted and the driver keeps the correction it already had
motorTune.withinScatter: Harmonic {h}: the best correction gained less than this order's own capture-to-capture scatter ({spread}), so it is not adopted and the harmonic stays disabled
motorTune.summaryNone: No correction improved the vibration — the driver is left uncorrected
motorTune.resultCodes: The corrections below are active now. “Save to config.g” writes them there to make them permanent, or add them yourself:
motorTune.resultCodesPhaseStepping: The corrections below are active now. “Save to config.g” writes them there to make them permanent (after the M970 that puts this driver into phase stepping, where the run needed it), or add them yourself after that command or closed loop setup:
motorTune.unsupported: This driver did not accept a waveform correction — check it supports a TMC5160/TMC2240 sine table and try again.
motorTune.speedTooHigh: At this speed the motor's full-step frequency is {hz} Hz, too high for the accelerometer to measure — reduce the speed to {speed} mm/s or below.

multi.headline: Per-axis resonance
multi.note: The recommendation above already weighs every axis at once — the per-axis figures below are for comparison, or to deliberately target one axis instead.
multi.agree: Every axis already agreed on this shaper and frequency independently.

config.scopeBody: RRF has one input shaper for the whole machine — choose whether this replaces it for every tool, or only re-asserts it each time this tool is picked up.
config.scopeAllHint: Writes the machine-wide M593 into config.g.
config.scopeToolHint: Writes M593 into {tool}'s own tool-change macro, re-sent every time it's picked up.
config.accelScopeBody: RRF supports only one active accelerometer at a time — choose whether this becomes the boot-time default regardless of which tool is mounted, or is only reactivated each time this tool is picked up.
config.accelScopeAllHint: Makes this the accelerometer RRF activates at startup, regardless of which tool is mounted. This is not "usable by every tool" — it's the boot-time default, and the only thing keeping any other accelerometer active.
config.accelScopeToolHint: Reactivates this accelerometer every time {tool} is physically picked up — a hardware check, plus a CAN round-trip for a toolboard — for the rest of this machine's life, whether or not you're testing that day.
config.backupNote: The original file is backed up alongside it before anything is written.
config.appendedNote: No existing {code} line was found in {file} — this appends a new one.
config.disabledDuplicateNote: There's also a commented-out {code} line in {file} — it stays disabled, but is easy to mistake for the current setting.
config.restartHint: RRF only re-reads config.g on a full restart, or if you tell it to run config.g again.

migration.banner: {count} accelerometer line(s) are still set in a tool's own tpost file - on this firmware that can silently override config.g's own slot assignment the next time that tool is picked up.
migration.title: Consolidate accelerometer setup into config.g
migration.body: Move {from} into {to}, each with its own slot. This is a one-time cleanup: from then on, each board's wiring lives in config.g instead of being re-asserted (and possibly overridden) on every tool change.

spectrum.heading: Frequency response (calibration / excite)
spectrum.body: The curve shows how strongly the toolhead vibrates at each frequency while it is driven across the band. Each hump is a resonance; the tallest one limits print quality. The recommended input shaper is tuned to cancel that main peak — the dashed line is the shaper's response (how much it lets through at each frequency) and the shaded 'after shaper' curve is what remains once it is applied. A good result flattens the big peak without raising vibration elsewhere. 'Show X/Y/Z channels' overlays each raw axis the accelerometer recorded (dotted lines) alongside the combined curve the recommendation actually runs on — useful for spotting vibration leaking into an axis you didn't mean to excite.

spectrogram.heading: Spectrogram (time vs frequency)
spectrogram.body: Switch to this view (or use Excite one frequency) to see how the vibration response changes over the course of the test — time runs left to right, frequency runs bottom to top, and brightness shows how strongly the toolhead is vibrating. A real resonance shows up as a horizontal band that stays at the same frequency throughout; a diagonal streak that moves with time is just the sweep's own excitation frequency passing through, not a real resonance.

belts.heading: Belt tension (CoreXY)
belts.body: The two belts are excited separately and overlaid. Curves that sit on top of each other mean the belts are matched. If one curve is the same shape but scaled up or down, the belts are at different tensions — adjust and re-test. If the curves have different shapes or peaks, the difference is mechanical (a bearing, idler or belt path), not tension.

profile.heading: Vibration vs speed
profile.body: Vibration energy is measured across a range of travel speeds. Tall points are speeds that hit a resonance; avoid those feedrates (or fix the underlying resonance with input shaping) and prefer the quieter speeds.

captures.title: Captured data
captures.hint: Tick one capture to view it, both belt files to compare tension, or several axis sweeps to overlay them.
captures.needBeltPair: Belt comparison needs both a Belt A and a Belt B capture — tick one of each.

results.headline: Apply {shaper} {'@'} {freq} Hz — removes ~{reduction}% of ringing
results.quietDetail: This capture shows no ringing worth shaping — either the machine is already well behaved, or the test didn't excite it. Try the frequency sweep method.
results.applied: {shaper} {'@'} {freq} Hz applied (M593). Add it to config.g to keep it after restarts.
results.verified: Verified with {shaper} {'@'} {freq} Hz: {reduction}% of vibration energy removed.

panel.noData: No measurements yet — open the lab to run one.

runningTask: Running {task} — keep clear, the machine is moving.

cancel.notice: Stopping after the current move finishes — RRF can't interrupt motion already in progress without a full emergency stop, so the machine will complete whatever it's doing right now.
cancel.title: Measurement cancelled
cancel.notification: Stopped before starting any further step. The machine finished whatever move was already in progress.

confirmGcode.title: Run custom G-code?
confirmGcode.body: This will run the following G-code on your machine with the recorder armed. Review it before continuing:

sweep.title: Calibrate input shaping
sweep.blurb: Sweeps the selected axis — or several at once, overlaid for comparison — through a frequency band and recommends the input shaper (M593) that removes the most ringing.
sweep.run: Moves each selected axis back and forth near its centre · all axes must be homed

belts.title: Belt tension (CoreXY)
belts.blurb: Excites the two CoreXY belts in turn (the X+Y and X−Y diagonals) and compares their resonance. Matched belts overlap; a tension imbalance scales one curve; a different shape points to a mechanical fault rather than tension.
belts.run: Moves both belts diagonally near the centre · CoreXY kinematics only

profile.title: Vibration vs speed
profile.blurb: Runs the axis at a range of speeds and measures vibration at each one, flagging the speed bands that excite a resonance so you can avoid them in your slicer.
profile.run: Constant-speed passes on the selected axis · all axes must be homed

axescheck.title: Accelerometer orientation
axescheck.blurb: Works out how the accelerometer is mounted relative to the machine axes and suggests the M955 I parameter so X, Y and Z read in the right directions.
axescheck.run: One sharp move per horizontal axis · all axes must be homed

motor.title: Motor quality
motor.blurb: Runs one motor at a range of constant speeds and measures vibration at multiples of its full-step frequency — full-step ripple, coil current imbalance and current-waveform distortion all show up at different orders. Only Z is testable on non-core kinematics, and its low step rate couples poorly to the accelerometer.
motor.axisNote: Tests one motor at a time
motor.run: Constant-speed passes driving one motor · all axes must be homed

motortune.title: Motor tuning (phase stepping)
motortune.blurb: Phase-stepping waveform tuning: searches for the current-waveform correction that minimises one motor's vibration, then writes it to the driver (M970.3 in phase-stepping mode, or the driver's sine table otherwise). Input shaping is disabled and the machine moves repeatedly while this runs.
motortune.axisNote: Tunes one motor at a time
motortune.run: Repeated round-trip passes driving one motor while probing corrections · all axes must be homed

excite.title: Excite one frequency
excite.blurb: Drives the axis at a single fixed frequency and shows the response over time as a spectrogram — handy for studying a suspicious peak found during calibration.
excite.run: Oscillates the selected axis at the chosen frequency near its centre

move.title: Quick test move
move.blurb: A single out-and-back move with the recorder armed — a fast resonance check without the full sweep. Less thorough than calibration, but quick.
move.run: One out-and-back move on the selected axis near its centre

custom.title: Custom move profile
custom.blurb: Records while running your own G-code moves — for non-standard tests or reproducing a specific motion. One move per line.
custom.run: Runs the G-code you supply with the recorder armed around it

captureTimeout: The accelerometer never reported a completed recording — check that it is configured and reachable, then try again.
